methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $42M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Tutor Intelligence is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Alon Kosowsky-Sachs and Josh Gruenstein that has raised $42.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine peers—one public and eight private—spanning robotics and manufacturing, including later-stage companies such as Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and earlier-stage players like Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses total capital raised as a proxy valuation base and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, implying $85M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The peer cohort spans both Series B and Seed stages, introducing stage heterogeneity; however, the median reflects market pricing for robotics companies at and near Tutor Intelligence's development phase.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $72M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $892M. This wide dispersion reflects tension between early-stage capital-proxy methods and later-stage peer comparables. Key uncertainties include revenue traction, capital efficiency relative to peers, and whether near-term funding will occur at earlier or later-stage valuations.
